exposure: Maternal care deserts (travel time and distance to obstetric and gynecological care)
cohort: The study included residents of North Carolina from 2016 to 2021.
finding: Increased travel times and distances to clinical care were associated with higher rates of adverse maternal and infant health outcomes, including severe maternal morbidity, preterm birth, and gestational diabetes.
mod_finding: Increased travel times and distances to clinical care were associated with higher cesarean delivery rates.
